question: In which country was FIFA founded?
answer: France; FIFA was founded in Paris on 21 May 1904.
facts: • FIFA stands for Fédération Internationale de Football Association. • Its headquarters is in Zürich, Switzerland.

question: When did Humayun rule?
facts: • Sher Shah Suri displaced Humayun in 1540. • Humayun regained Delhi in 1555 and died in 1556.

question: Which country is the world’s largest tea producer?
answer: China.
facts: • India is also among the leading tea producers. • Kenya is a major exporter of black tea; production and export rankings are different measures.

question: What does NATO stand for?
answer: North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
facts: • NATO is a collective-defence alliance. • The founding treaty was signed in Washington, D.C.

question: Who received Nishan-e-Haider for the 1965 war?
answer: Major Raja Aziz Bhatti Shaheed.
facts: • He was martyred while defending the Lahore front in September 1965. • Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan’s highest military gallantry award.

question: Who was Pakistan’s first Prime Minister?
answer: Liaquat Ali Khan.
facts: • He served from 1947 to 1951. • Khawaja Nazimuddin succeeded him as Prime Minister.

question: Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan?
answer: Mir Sarfraz Bugti (subject to current confirmation).
facts: • Quetta is the provincial capital. • For current-affairs exams, verify the office-holder close to the test.

question: What is Türkiye’s currency?
answer: Turkish lira (TRY).
facts: • Currency symbols: ■ for lira. • Türkiye’s central bank is based in Ankara.

question: What is the world’s fastest bird?
answer: Peregrine falcon, in a hunting dive (stoop).
facts: • Its diving speed can exceed 300 km/h under certain conditions. • It is not the fastest bird in level flight.

question: Who passed the Objectives Resolution?
answer: It was moved by Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan and passed by Pakistan's Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.
facts: • It was presented on 7 March 1949. • It set out principles for Pakistan's future constitution, including democracy, freedom, equality and social justice within an Islamic framework.

question: When did Khalid ibn al-Walid accept Islam?
answer: Around 8 AH (628 CE), before the Conquest of Makkah.
facts: • He later became a leading Muslim commander and was known as Sayfullah (“Sword of Allah”). • The exact date is usually given in seerah chronology as 8 AH.

question: How many agencies did the former FATA consist of?
answer: Seven tribal agencies.
facts: • The seven agencies were Bajaur, Khyber, Kurram, Mohmand, Orakzai, North Waziristan and South Waziristan. • FATA was merged into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018; it is no longer a separate federal territory.

question: Who is the Governor of Sindh?
answer: Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi (as displayed by the Governor of Sindh website on 14 October 2026).
facts: • This is a date-sensitive current-affairs question. • The Governor is the constitutional head of the province; the Chief Minister leads the provincial government.

question: What is Pakistan's highest civil award?
answer: Nishan-e-Pakistan.
facts: • It is Pakistan's highest civilian award. • It may be conferred on Pakistani citizens and foreign nationals for distinguished service.

question: Which words can be synonyms of “prescribe”?
answer: Order, direct or specify; in medicine, it can mean to authorize a treatment or medicine.
facts: • “Prescribe” and “proscribe” have opposite meanings: prescribe means recommend/order; proscribe means forbid. • Choose the synonym that best fits the sentence.

question: Who was Pakistan's first Foreign Minister?
answer: Sir Muhammad Zafrullah Khan.
facts: • He was Pakistan's first foreign minister after independence. • He later served as President of the UN General Assembly and a judge of the International Court of Justice.

question: Which continent has historically been called the “Dark Continent”?
answer: Africa (a dated historical label, not a scientific description).
facts: • The phrase arose in European colonial-era writing and is now considered outdated. • Africa is the world's second-largest continent by area and population.

question: What is the name of the Pakistan-Afghanistan border?
answer: The Durand Line.
facts: • It was agreed in 1893. • The boundary remains politically contentious in Afghanistan-Pakistan relations.

question: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
answer: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-e-Azam).
facts: • He served from 14 August 1947 until his death on 11 September 1948. • “Governor-General” is different from a provincial governor.

question: Who is associated with the title “Atiq”?
answer: Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA) is traditionally associated with the title “Atiq”.
facts: • He is best known by the title Al-Siddiq. • He was the first Caliph after Prophet Muhammad (PBUH).

question: For what did Malala Yousafzai receive the Nobel Prize?
answer: The Nobel Peace Prize in 2014, for her struggle against the suppression of children and young people and for the right of all children to education.
facts: • She shared the prize with Kailash Satyarthi. • Malala was the youngest Nobel Prize laureate at the time of the award.

question: What percentage of Pakistan's land area is classified as forest?
answer: The World Bank's forest-area indicator reports about 4.6% for Pakistan in 2023; the submitted 1.91% figure is not the current World Bank measure.
facts: • Forest-area percentages differ by definition, inventory and year. • Use a named source and reference year in exam notes instead of mixing estimates.

question: Which planet is nearest to Earth?
answer: Venus can come closest to Earth at its closest approach; Mercury is the nearest planet on average over time. The question must specify the definition.
facts: • School MCQs commonly expect Venus for closest approach. • Astronomers distinguish minimum approach distance from average distance over time.

question: Who was the first woman Chief Justice of a High Court in Pakistan?
answer: Justice Syeda Tahira Safdar, appointed Chief Justice of the Balochistan High Court in 2018.
facts: • She was the first woman to head a Pakistani High Court. • She retired in 2019.

question: What is a major immediate energy source for an athlete?
answer: Carbohydrates are a major readily available energy source, especially during high-intensity exercise.
facts: • Carbohydrates are stored as glycogen in muscles and the liver. • Fat and, to a smaller extent, protein also contribute to energy metabolism.

question: On what date was the Objectives Resolution introduced in the Constituent Assembly?
answer: 7 March 1949; it was passed on 12 March 1949.
facts: • Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan moved the resolution. • Question 1 asks about the passing date; this item asks the introduction date.

question: What was France's currency before the euro?
answer: The French franc.
facts: • France adopted the euro for electronic transactions in 1999 and euro banknotes/coins in 2002. • One euro replaced 6.55957 French francs at the fixed conversion rate.

question: Who is associated with the residency at Ziarat?
answer: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
facts: • The Quaid-e-Azam Residency is in Ziarat, Balochistan. • Jinnah stayed there in 1948 during his final illness.

question: When was the Jinnah Antarctic Research Station established?
answer: 18 January 1991.
facts: • The station was established during Pakistan's Antarctic expedition. • Pakistan later became an associate member of the Scientific Committee on Antarctic Research in 1992.

question: Who said of the Prophet (PBUH), “His character was the Quran”?
answer: Hazrat Aisha (RA), describing the Prophet's character when asked about it.
facts: • The report is found in hadith collections, including Sahih Muslim. • The statement describes his character as embodying Quranic teachings.

question: Which well-known body of water is famous for its very high salinity?
answer: The Dead Sea, technically a hypersaline lake rather than a true sea.
facts: • It lies between Jordan and the West Bank/Israel region. • Some smaller hypersaline lakes can have higher salinity, so “most saline water on Earth” is not universally true.

question: Amjad and Ahmed have 24 balloons in total. If Amjad has three times as many as Ahmed, how many does Amjad have?
answer: 18 balloons, assuming Amjad:Ahmed = 3:1.
facts: • Let Ahmed have x and Amjad 3x; then 4x = 24, so x = 6. • Amjad has 3 × 6 = 18 balloons.
